disclaimer: This is an investigation indicator based on observed network data. It does not confirm a vulnerability, an attack or a compromise.

context.EXPECTED: Device role '{role}' normally includes this service, so the finding is weighted lower.
context.UNEXPECTED: Device role '{role}' does not normally include this service, so the finding is weighted higher.
context.UNKNOWN: No device role is set for this device, so ThreatMesh cannot tell whether this service is expected here.
context.UNKNOWN_SERVICE: The service could not be identified, so ThreatMesh cannot tell whether it is expected for role '{role}'.

generic_service.why_it_matters: {service} ({category}) adds to what the device exposes on the network. Whether that is appropriate depends on the device's purpose.
generic_service.recommended_state: The service is offered only where the device's purpose requires it and is reachable only from networks that need it.
investigate: Who owns this device and what is its purpose?
Was this service enabled intentionally?
do_not: Do not attempt to log in, guess credentials or exploit the service.
Do not disable it before confirming that nothing depends on it.
mitigation: Disable the service if it is not needed.
Restrict access to trusted hosts or segments where it is needed.

NEW_DEVICE.summary: Device was not observed during previous authorized scans.
NEW_DEVICE.what_happened: A device with IP {ip} (MAC {mac}, vendor {vendor}) appeared in scan #{scan}. It was not observed in earlier authorized scans.
NEW_DEVICE.why_it_matters: A new device can be harmless (a phone, a guest device, new equipment), but it changes who can reach the network, so its owner and purpose should be known.
NEW_DEVICE.how_detected: Device identity (MAC address, or IP address when no MAC was visible) was compared with all earlier scans and no match was found.
NEW_DEVICE.recommended_state: Every device on the network has a known owner and purpose.
investigate: Who owns this device and why is it connected?
Do the vendor and hostname match what you would expect?
Is it a guest, an employee device or new network equipment?
do_not: Do not assume the device is malicious.
Do not probe or block it intrusively before verifying ownership.
mitigation: Record the device in the asset inventory if it is legitimate.
Move it to a guest or separate segment if it should not reach internal resources.

DEVICE_OFFLINE.summary: Device was observed in the previous scan but not in this one.
DEVICE_OFFLINE.what_happened: The device at {ip} (MAC {mac}) seen in scan #{prev_scan} was not observed in scan #{scan}.
DEVICE_OFFLINE.why_it_matters: Devices go offline for ordinary reasons (powered off, out of range, asleep). A device that should always be available and disappears may need attention.
DEVICE_OFFLINE.how_detected: The device lists of two consecutive scans with the same target scope were compared.
DEVICE_OFFLINE.recommended_state: Always-on devices stay visible; mobile devices appear intermittently.
investigate: Is the device expected to be on at scan time?
Was the scan scope or timing different?
Could host discovery have missed it?
do_not: Do not assume failure or compromise from a single missed scan.
mitigation: Repeat the scan to confirm before acting.
Check power and connectivity of devices that should be always on.

IP_CHANGED.summary: Same device identity observed with a different IP address.
IP_CHANGED.what_happened: A device identified by MAC {mac} was seen at {previous_ip} earlier and at {current_ip} in scan #{scan}.
IP_CHANGED.why_it_matters: IP changes are common with DHCP leases. Repeated or unexpected changes can point to address conflicts or configuration problems.
IP_CHANGED.how_detected: The same device identity (MAC address) was matched across scans and its IP address differed.
IP_CHANGED.recommended_state: Devices that must be reachable at a fixed address use a DHCP reservation or a static address.
investigate: Is the DHCP lease time short?
Did the device move to another access point or segment?
do_not: Do not treat an IP change alone as suspicious.
mitigation: Use DHCP reservations for infrastructure devices and printers.
Key the asset inventory by MAC address rather than IP address.

NEW_PORT.what_happened: Port {port}/{protocol} ({service}) is open on {ip}. It was not open in scan #{prev_scan}.
NEW_PORT.why_it_matters: Each open port is a reachable entry point. A new one means the exposed surface of the device changed, which may be intentional (software installed, service enabled) or unplanned.
NEW_PORT.how_detected: Open ports of the same device identity were compared between scan #{prev_scan} and scan #{scan}.
NEW_PORT.recommended_state: Open ports match the device's purpose and are documented.
investigate: Was software installed or a service enabled on the device recently?
Is this a service the device is expected to offer?
do_not: Do not attempt to log in, guess credentials or exploit the service to verify it.
mitigation: Disable the service if it is not needed.
Restrict access to trusted hosts or segments if it is needed.

CLOSED_PORT.what_happened: Port {port}/{protocol} ({service}) was open on {ip} in scan #{prev_scan} and is not open in scan #{scan}.
CLOSED_PORT.why_it_matters: A closed port can mean a service was stopped on purpose, stopped unexpectedly or is temporarily filtered. If the service was needed, this can be an availability issue.
CLOSED_PORT.how_detected: Open ports of the same device identity were compared between scan #{prev_scan} and scan #{scan}.
CLOSED_PORT.recommended_state: Changes to open ports are intentional and recorded.
investigate: Was the service stopped intentionally?
Does anything depend on it?
do_not: Do not restart or reconfigure the service remotely without authorization.
mitigation: Update the documented baseline if the change was intentional.
Restore the service through the normal change process if it was closed unintentionally.

NEW_SERVICE.what_happened: Service {service} ({ports}) was detected on {ip}. This service type was not detected on the device in scan #{prev_scan}.
NEW_SERVICE.why_it_matters: A service type the device did not offer before changes what the device does on the network. It can be legitimate (new software) or unplanned.
NEW_SERVICE.how_detected: Service names reported by Nmap service detection were compared between scan #{prev_scan} and scan #{scan} for the same device identity.
NEW_SERVICE.recommended_state: The services a device offers match its purpose and are documented.
investigate: Was software installed or enabled on the device recently?
Is this a service the device is expected to offer?
do_not: Do not attempt to log in, guess credentials or exploit the service to verify it.
mitigation: Disable the service if it is not needed.
Restrict access to trusted hosts or segments if it is needed.

SERVICE_REMOVED.what_happened: Service {service} ({ports}) detected on {ip} in scan #{prev_scan} was not detected in scan #{scan}.
SERVICE_REMOVED.why_it_matters: A removed service can be an intended cleanup, a stopped process or a detection difference between scans.
SERVICE_REMOVED.how_detected: Service names reported by Nmap service detection were compared between scan #{prev_scan} and scan #{scan}.
SERVICE_REMOVED.recommended_state: Service changes are intentional and recorded.
investigate: Was the service stopped or removed on purpose?
Does anything depend on it?
do_not: Do not restart or reconfigure the service remotely without authorization.
mitigation: Update the documented baseline if the change was intentional.
Restore the service through the normal change process if it was removed unintentionally.

SERVICE_VERSION_CHANGED.what_happened: The version reported for {service} on {ip} port {port}/{protocol} changed from '{previous}' to '{current}' between scan #{prev_scan} and scan #{scan}.
SERVICE_VERSION_CHANGED.why_it_matters: Version changes usually mean software was updated or replaced. Updates are normally good; unexpected changes or downgrades should be understood. Nmap version detection relies on banners and can be inaccurate.
SERVICE_VERSION_CHANGED.how_detected: Product and version strings reported by Nmap service detection were compared for the same port.
SERVICE_VERSION_CHANGED.recommended_state: Software runs a supported, maintained version and changes are recorded.
investigate: Was this a planned update?
Is the new version supported and maintained?
do_not: Do not assume a version is vulnerable without checking the vendor's advisories.
mitigation: Keep software on supported versions.
Record the new version in the baseline.

EXPOSED_SERVICE.how_detected: The open port and service name were reported by Nmap service detection in scan #{scan}. The weighting comes from ThreatMesh rules and the device role.

UNKNOWN_SERVICE.what_happened: Port {port}/{protocol} on {ip} is open but Nmap could not identify the service.
UNKNOWN_SERVICE.why_it_matters: Unidentified services are harder to assess. They may be custom software, an unusual protocol or a vendor management interface.
UNKNOWN_SERVICE.how_detected: Nmap service detection returned no service name for this port in scan #{scan}.
UNKNOWN_SERVICE.recommended_state: Every open port maps to a known, documented service.
investigate: Which software on the device listens on this port?
Is it a vendor specific management or application port?
Does the device documentation mention it?
do_not: Do not send crafted or fuzzed traffic to identify it.
Do not attempt to authenticate to the service.
mitigation: Identify the service through the device owner or vendor documentation.
Close or restrict the port if it is not needed.

MULTIPLE_REMOTE_ACCESS.summary: Multiple remote access services on one device.
MULTIPLE_REMOTE_ACCESS.why_it_matters: Each remote access service is a separate way to reach the device. More of them means more places to configure, update and monitor.
MULTIPLE_REMOTE_ACCESS.how_detected: Detected services in the REMOTE_ACCESS category were counted for this device in scan #{scan}.
MULTIPLE_REMOTE_ACCESS.recommended_state: Only the remote access methods that are actually needed are enabled, restricted to trusted hosts.
investigate: Which of these services is actually used?
Are they restricted to administrative hosts?
do_not: Do not attempt to log in or test credentials.
Do not disable all of them at once without another way to administer the device.
mitigation: Disable the remote access services that are not used.
Restrict the remaining ones to trusted hosts or a management segment.
